medications.purpose: Lower clinic blood pressure to <140/90 mmHg (stage 2 hypertension control)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 recommends a calcium‑channel blocker as first‑line therapy for patients aged ≥55 years or of Afro‑Caribbean ethnicity (preferred amlodipine) (first_line_treatment).

assumptions_warnings: eGFR, serum potassium, and urine ACR are not available – assumed normal for initiating amlodipine; renal function will be checked before any future ACE‑I/ARB addition.
Allergy status unknown – will verify no ACE‑I, ARB, or sulfonamide allergy before future prescribing.
Age not explicitly recorded – assumed ≥55 y or Afro‑Caribbean ethnicity based on guideline indication.
BMI, smoking status, alcohol intake, and QRISK score are missing – these will be obtained to guide lifestyle advice and statin eligibility.
Blood pressure target may be lower (<130/80 mmHg) if significant proteinuria or CKD is later identified – will reassess after investigations.
treatment_summary: Start amlodipine 5 mg daily as first‑line antihypertensive therapy for this Black male with stage 2 hypertension, per NICE NG136. No current drug interactions or contraindications. Arrange baseline labs (eGFR, electrolytes, urine ACR, lipid profile, HbA1c) and lifestyle measures (salt <6 g/day, DASH diet, 150 min/week exercise, weight management, limit alcohol, smoking cessation). Review BP in 2 weeks and again at 4–6 weeks; if still ≥140/90 mmHg, consider adding an ACE‑I/ARB after confirming renal function and potassium. Refer for obstructive sleep apnea assessment and CPAP therapy.
